\section[la facoltà]{la facoltà — the faculty (of a university); the ability}

\label{lesson:IT-C380-facolta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the school report, then the Italian for the head teacher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la facoltà}
\textbf{la facoltà} — \textquotedblleft{}the faculty (of a university); the ability\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Studio alla facoltà di lettere.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I study in the arts faculty.}
\end{quote}

Also a power or ability: \emph{la facoltà di scegliere}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{facoltà} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{facultās} \textquotedblleft{}ability, power, means\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), related to \emph{facilis} \textquotedblleft{}easy to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la facoltà}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la facoltà}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la facoltà}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the school report, then the Italian for the head teacher, then say \emph{la facoltà} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la facoltà mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The faculty (of a university); the ability\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la matricola]{la matricola — the first-year student; the registration number}

\label{lesson:IT-C380-matricola}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the head teacher, then the Italian for the faculty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la matricola}
\textbf{la matricola} — \textquotedblleft{}the first-year student; the registration number\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le matricole hanno lezione nell'aula grande.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The first-year students have lessons in the big lecture hall.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La matricola} is also your student number. One form for men and women.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{matricola} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{mātrīcula} \textquotedblleft{}a public register\textquotedblright{}, diminutive of \emph{mātrīx} \textquotedblleft{}a register, a womb\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{māter} \textquotedblleft{}mother\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la matricola}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the head teacher, then the Italian for the faculty, then say \emph{la matricola} again
\end{itemize}

\section[iscriversi]{iscriversi — to enrol, to sign up}

\label{lesson:IT-C380-iscriversi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the faculty, then the Italian for the first-year student.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: iscriversi}
\textbf{iscriversi} — \textquotedblleft{}to enrol, to sign up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se ti iscrivi entro settembre, paghi meno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you enrol by September, you pay less.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Iscriversi a} — to sign up for: \emph{a un corso}, \emph{in palestra}. Past participle \emph{iscritto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{iscriversi} comes from Latin \emph{īnscrībere} \textquotedblleft{}to write on, to enter in a list\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{in} and \emph{scrībere} \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}: you put your name on the list.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'iscrizione]{l'iscrizione — the enrolment, the registration; the inscription}

\label{lesson:IT-C380-iscrizione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the first-year student, then the Italian for to enrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'iscrizione}
\textbf{l'iscrizione} — \textquotedblleft{}the enrolment, the registration; the inscription\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'iscrizione costa cento euro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Registration costs a hundred euros.}
\end{quote}

On a stone or a monument, it is an inscription.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{iscrizione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{īnscrīptiō} \textquotedblleft{}a writing on, an inscription\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{īnscrībere}, built on \emph{scrībere} \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il semestre]{il semestre — the semester, the half-year}

\label{lesson:IT-C380-semestre}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to enrol, then the Italian for the enrolment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il semestre}
\textbf{il semestre} — \textquotedblleft{}the semester, the half-year\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nel secondo semestre ho meno lezioni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the second semester I have fewer lessons.}
\end{quote}

Six months; a \emph{trimestre} is three.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{semestre} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sēmestris} \textquotedblleft{}of six months\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{sex} \textquotedblleft{}six\textquotedblright{} and \emph{mēnsis} \textquotedblleft{}month\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
